trigger: a different local user creates /tmp/yuzu-uat/pids first and plants a PID record (a victim-visible PID, an identity that is a substring of that process's command line, its ps lstart), then the operator runs start or stop
classification_rationale: the change promises that only processes this script recorded are signalled, but a record planted by another user was believed; the old pgrep -f code could only hit command-line matches, so the new record path widened the attacker-steerable kill (probes: PID 1 command and start time readable, 484 children). Native band HIGH; derived CRITICAL (I1 raised by E2); gates either way
summary: PID records were trusted without provenance. Found independently by security-guardian, quality-engineer/unhappy-path and docs/compliance. Fixed in 24e51c06b: records are believed only from directories owned by the invoking user and not group/other-writable, as regular non-symlink files owned by that user, naming a PID above 1; an untrusted record is never signalled or deleted (and, per 28a724868, makes stop and start refuse); prepare_fresh_run refuses a foreign directory that survived the wipe. Gate-8 re-review CLEAN.

trigger: a stack started by the pre-change script is still up (it has no PID records); the first start or stop after upgrading
classification_rationale: the refusal told the operator to stop the stack from the session that owns it, which cannot work for a stack that has no records
summary: One-time migration refusal was misleading. Fixed in 24e51c06b: the refusal names the by-hand route for a stack that predates PID records, docs/uat-environment.md and the changelog fragment say so, and the PR body repeats it.

trigger: stop run while a PID record is untrusted (another uid, or a directory left group-writable by an older script)
classification_rationale: stop printed that the stack was stopped while a possibly live port-less agent could remain. Reporter's native band LOW (an operator-visible warning precedes the message); the derivation from I3 + E4 gives HIGH, which governs the gate, so it is recorded BLOCKING and was fixed before the PR
summary: An untrusted record returned 'nothing to stop'. Fixed in 28a724868: it now counts as a stop failure, so start and stop refuse with exit 1; the two tests assert rc 1 and were mutation-checked.

trigger: reading docs/uat-environment.md line 18 on a host with ss but no lsof; the 15433 refusal
classification_rationale: docs overstated that holders are reported via lsof and omitted the Postgres host-port refusal
summary: Two real wording gaps fixed in 24e51c06b. Other items rejected with evidence by the Architect: the docs already name the exit code and start time; SKILL.md quotes a verbatim substring of the message; preflight.sh, perf-sample.sh and perf-gate.sh are outside this PR.
